Engineering the  
Future of Performance
Engineering finds its true meaning in the making. 
Built on a century-long engineering foundation, KOEL continues to translate ideas into 
impactful solutions through focused in -house R&D in India and a deep commitment 
to indigenous development. The spirit of 'Made in Kirloskar' reflects our identity 
of celebrating the craft of engineering, the skill of our people, and the quiet act of 
building for the nation. 
As we move forward, we firm up our commitment to shaping a self -reliant, 
innovation -led future that supports the vision of Make-in-India.MADE IN KIRLOSKAR

Blending tech finesse  
with market relevance
Our advanced engineering capabilities span a 
comprehensive portfolio of air-cooled and liquid-
cooled engines ranging from 3 kVA to 12,000 kVA, 
enabling us to serve applications of every scale and 
complexity. From industrial operations and critical 
infrastructure specialised power needs, we deliver 
customised solutions designed for performance, 
durability and efficiency.
Driven by dedicated Corporate Research & 
Engineering (CRE) and Application Engineering (AE) 
divisions, our innovation ecosystem is focused on 
anticipating the future. We engineer application-
specific solutions, blending technical precision with 
market relevance for specific requirements. This 
helps us stay agile in a world of spiralling demand  
for performance.
Sustainability is integral to our vision. Our portfolio 
includes emission-compliant and environmentally 
responsible technologies, while our leadership in 
alternative fuels such as biodiesel, natural gas, 
HFEC* and biogas-based engines, underscores our 
commitment to cleaner energy pathways. We are 
also advancing fuel-agnostic and hybrid genset 
technologies that offer greater flexibility, resilience 
and lower environmental impact.Digital intelligence is redefining performance, and 
Kirloskar is at the forefront of this transformation. 
Through IoT-enabled gensets, predictive remote 
monitoring systems, microgrid solutions and 
intelligent controllers such as Optiprime, we are 
helping customers optimise uptime, efficiency and 
control.
Our engineering ambit has a robust after-sales 
system supported by an extensive service and 
distribution network. Whether enabling high-
horsepower industrial applications or empowering 
farmers with accessible mechanisation solutions, 
we remain committed to engineering outcomes that 
create lasting value.
As we move forward, Kirloskar Oil Engines Limited 
continues to engineer the future of performance, 
with innovation in our thinking, sustainability in our 
approach, and trust in everything proudly Made in 
Kirloskar.
* Hydrogen Fuel Enhanced Combination

CONTENTS About the report
We are pleased to present our Annual Report which 
includes voluntary information to the extent available 
to us, in accordance with the reporting framework 
developed and designed by International Integrated 
Reporting Council (IIRC). 
This report is primarily intended to address the 
information requirements of investors (our equity and 
prospective investors). Our endeavour is to present 
this information in a manner that is also relevant to all 
the key stakeholders. This report also aligns with the 
Companies Act, 2013, Indian Accounting Standards 
and SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015.Scope and boundary
This report provides comprehensive information about the business 
activities of Kirloskar Oil Engines Limited (KOEL), suitably communicated 
through the six strategic goals  as per the guidelines defined by the 
International Integrated Reporting Council (IIRC). 
The document encapsulates our business model, overarching performance 
and corresponding results. It is important to note that the financial capital 
parameters discussed in this report pertain exclusively to ‘Kirloskar Oil 
Engines Limited’ on a standalone operation.
Reporting period
The major reporting period for the Annual Report is April 1st, 2025 to 
March 31st, 2026. However, certain portions of the report provide facts and 
numbers from prior years in order to give readers a complete picture.
Assurance for financial statements
To ensure the integrity of facts and information, the financial statements 
are audited by M/s. G. D. Apte & Co., Chartered Accountants. In addition, 
the ‘Independent Auditor’s Report’ has been duly incorporated as part of 
this report.
Stakeholder engagement and materiality 
Stakeholder consultation is central to KOEL 's approach to identifying and 
managing material topics, risks and opportunities. Following a materiality 
reassessment in CY 25, stakeholder engagement was carried out primarily 
through structured surveys, designed to capture perceptions on the 
importance of identified environmental, social and governance topics. Inputs 
received through the stakeholder engagement process were analysed using 
a defined scoring to develop a materiality matrix that continues to guide 
KOEL 's evolving Sustainability Strategy 2030.

Combined market capitalisation***Years of 
excellence
For over 137 years, the Kirloskar Group has served as a keystone of India’s industrial 
evolution. Its journey began in 1888 by a forward-thinking founder who transitioned 
from running a modest bicycle repair shop into creating the nation’s first iron plough, 
an act that laid the foundation for India’s industrial revolution. This pioneering spirit 
catalysed a legacy of progress that continues today. Today, the Group is a distinguished 
leader across multiple sectors—including internal combustion engines, power backup, 
castings, and pneumatic and cooling systems providing critical engineering solutions to 
a diverse global market.Engineering solutions for 
future generations
The Group provides the backbone of infrastructure across 
a wide variety of sectors, including hospitality, IT/ITES, 
agriculture, manufacturing, food and beverage, oil and gas, 
infrastructure, and real estate. Kirloskar’s remarkable growth 
and resilience are rooted in strong values that serve as the 
establishment for every one of its enterprises.
The Group’s journey began when the founder, Shri Laxmanrao 
Kirloskar, established an ordinary bicycle repair shop in 
Belgaum, Karnataka. This humble start soon transitioned 
into a machine tool workshop, where he created iron 
ploughs and chaff cutters, revolutionary examples of 
engineering advancements that would eventually define the 
Group’s trajectory.
KIRLOSKAR GROUP'S PHILOSOPHY
His son, Shri Shantanurao Laxmanrao Kirloskar, carried this 
legacy forward with visionary leadership, transforming the 
Kirloskar Group into one of India’s most respected industrial 
powerhouses. Under his expert guidance, the Group expanded 
into new sectors and international markets, solidifying the 
Company's reputation on the global stage. 
Today, Shri Laxmanrao Kirloskar is remembered as both 
a pioneer of Indian industry and a reformer dedicated to 
improving lives. His entrepreneurial spirit continues to provide 
opportunities for thousands across India and benefits millions 
more through the Group’s extensive global operations.About Kirloskar Group

As a key member of the Kirloskar Group, following the Group’s 
legacy, we offer an extensive portfolio of engines engineered for 
power generation and industrial use. Our solutions serve vital 
sectors, including construction, railways, marine, defence, and 
agriculture. Additionally, we provide pumps, motors, and related 
products to address a wide variety of customer needs.
*The Business to Customer (“B2C”) business segment of the Company was transferred by way of slump sale as a going concern to its wholly owned subsidiary,

financial performance, it reflected the strength of our strategy, the investments we have 
made in our people and products, and the opportunities emerging from India’s growth story.

being primarily construction and mining-dependent 
to a genuinely diversified portfolio spanning Defence, 
Nuclear, Marine, Railways, Construction and Mining.

a long-term supply relationship with the Indian Navy

the largest individual contracts in KOEL ’s history.

begun to yield significant results. We identify white 
spaces methodically, align our product capability 
to the requirement, and then pursue long-cycle 
strategic programmes with patience and rigour.Financial performance*

up 33%. EBITDA margins improved by 90 basis points 
to 13.10%. Net profit from continuing operations 
grew 35% to ₹ 464 crores. Consolidated revenues 
grew 22%. Our net cash position (post-debt, including 
treasury) stood at ₹ 552 crores. These are not 
numbers produced by a favourable cycle alone; they

culture built over nearly eight decades.

Structural actions: Sharpening focus 
for the next phase 
Two important corporate actions were completed in 
FY 25-26:
First, the transfer of our B2C business to our wholly 
owned subsidiary LGM via slump sale was effected 
from Q3 (now branded Kirloskar Fluid Dynamics). 
This sharpens KOEL ’s standalone focus on its B2B 
engineering and power generation core, while giving 
Kirloskar Fluid Dynamics — which delivered 10% 
domestic and 13% international growth in  
Q4 FY 25-26 and 36% international revenue growth 
for the full year — the dedicated management 
attention and operational structure suited to its 
distinct market dynamics.
Second, we incorporated Kirloskar Advanced 
Systems Pvt. Ltd. as a new subsidiary, focused on 
systems integration and advanced technology for 
defence and other strategic sectors. Carving this 
into a dedicated entity — with its own governance, 
culture, and accountability — allows us to attract 
specialised talent, and build intellectual property that 
is held separately. We will provide further updates on 
this entity as our programmes mature.

demand already at hand

investments at our Kagal manufacturing site 
investments driven by demand we are already 
experiencing, not by speculation:
Phase 1: ₹ 700 crores to add engine capacity across 
enhanced and new lines on the existing campus, 
coming online by April 2027. Phase 2: ₹ 1,400 crores 
over two years for an additional high-horsepower and 
specialised engines in a new building at the same site.

The space and variable load dilemma
Modern industrial facilities, commercial complexes and critical 
infrastructure increasingly face the challenge of meeting 
growing power requirements while operating within a limited 
space. Conventional standby power systems often require 
multiple large gensets and extensive installation spaces, making 
it difficult to deploy them in high-density urban developments, 
data centers and industrial facilities. 
Engineered to minimise space,  
maximise power
KOEL engineered the Optiprime series as an ultra-compact, 
export-grade power solution that delivers high output from a 
significantly reduced space, enabling customers to optimise 
valuable space without compromising reliability or performance.
At the heart of the Optiprime range lies its patented Twin Hybrid 
Power Pack architecture, which integrates two synchronised 
power cores within a single compact system. It maximises 
power density while reducing the space requirements. The 
hybrid architecture continuously monitors load conditions 
and automatically distributes power between the two cores 
to match the demand efficiently. The result is a solution that 
combines space optimisation, operational flexibility and built-
in redundancy. During maintenance or servicing of one power 
core, the other seamlessly supports critical loads, ensuring 
uninterrupted power availability.
Last-mile customisation
To meet diverse global compliance demands, KOEL engineered 
the complete system as a  highly flexible single-package asset. 
By consolidating power cores, internal synchronisation systems, 
and post-treatment exhaust into a single enclosure, the system 
simplifies international transportation and field installation. This 
compact design gives project  architects the freedom to execute 
last-mile site customisation, tailoring acoustic insulation for 
strict urban noise limits or tweaking layouts for irregular physical 
spaces. This modular adaptability makes it equally effective for 
urban commercial high-rises and remote, rural utilities.Green solutions and positive returns 
In an industrial landscape repurposed for decarbonisation, the 
Optiprime series proves that ecological responsibility can align 
with financial prudence. Fully compliant with advanced CPCB IV+ 
emission standards, the system relies on specialised emission 
control technology to minimise its environmental footprint. 
By keeping the engine within its optimal thermal efficiency 
band, the system delivers superior fuel economy. This massive 
reduction in operating expenditure (opex) directly accelerates 
recovery of capital expenditure (capex), offering global 
organisations a highly sustainable power solution with the 
shortest timeline for a positive ROI.Target applications
Data centers Healthcare
Logistics Hospitality RetailInfrastructure Manufacturing

Principles of risk management 
The following principles underpin our approach to risk management across the organisation:

decision-making

toleranceEvery business decision is taken with a thorough understanding of 
associated risks and a conscious acceptance of their implications.
Our risk approach is built to safeguard and strengthen business 
value by proactively addressing uncertainties and minimising 
potential adverse outcomes.
We foster a culture where every employee understands the risks 
relevant to their role and is equipped with the knowledge to address 
and manage them effectively.
The controls and measures we deploy are designed for sustained 
impact, embedded directly into our core business processes rather 
than treated as isolated interventions.
Our risk tolerance thresholds are periodically revisited and 
recalibrated to remain aligned with the evolving direction and 
priorities of the organisation.
All risk events — whether emerging, ongoing, or resolved — are 
reported in a timely manner, with appropriate and decisive action 
taken at each stage.Risk Management
Risk management is embedded across our operations and 
guides decision-making at every level.Converting uncertainties 
into opportunities
Our framework integrates both strategic and ground-level perspectives, underpinned by a rigorous internal control system 
continuously validated through audits and calibrated to our business's scale and complexity. Recognising risk as inherent to our 
environment, we balance foresight with preparedness. Our response is practical, responsive, and forward-looking: mapping exposures 
across business, operational, and strategic levels while embedding controls into every critical process.
The risk management policy is reviewed by the Board of Directors and updated as necessary once every two financial years, ensuring 
that it remains aligned with evolving industry dynamics and the organisation's growing complexity.

and decentralised system architectureRisk governance framework
Our risk management framework is structured around a multi-
tiered governance model. The Risk Management Committee, 
acting on behalf of the Board, holds the overall responsibility 
for formulating and overseeing the policy. One designated risk 
owner, drawn from the senior leadership team or a relevant 
business or function head, is assigned to each identified risk, 
supported by team members responsible for executing the 
mitigation plan. The head of internal audit is responsible for 
monitoring and ensuring adherence to all mitigation plans 
enterprise-wide.Risk assessment process
Our structured risk management process systematically 
identifies, assesses, monitors, and mitigates risks in consistence 
with our overall strategic direction. It covers significant risks 
across all levels of the organisation, adopting a balanced 
methodology that integrates both top-level and ground-level 
perspectives. Risks are reviewed on a continuous basis, with due 
consideration given to external developments that may influence

Management Committee and BoardLevel Key roles and responsibilitiesThe process is structured around three interconnected stages:
Risk identification and categorisation
Risks are identified using the COSO 
framework, adopting a top-down 
approach across four domains: strategic, 
operational, financial, and compliance, 
at both the enterprise and business 
unit levels.
Risk description
Each identified risk is documented in a 
structured format capturing the scope, 
nature, stakeholders affected, likely 
impact, and possible mitigation measures.
Risk estimation
The consequences of each risk 
occurrence are quantified using 
quantitative or qualitative techniques. 
Probability is assigned from very high 
to very low, and risks are classified as 
high, medium, or low based on the cost 
impact analysis.
These stages operate as a continuous, integrated cycle, ensuring 
that the risks are understood, tracked, and managed across the 
entire organisation.

Execution programme68 monthsThe evolution of zero-error engineering 
This ability to deliver highly customised solutions across 
infrastructure, rail, and metro networks serves as the operational 
baseline for our most critical mission. KOEL achieves this by 
taking absolute, end-to-end ownership of the entire engineering 
solution stack in-house. By cross-pollinating these complex 
capabilities across diverse business verticals, the same 
engineering discipline that guarantees uptime in high-density 
urban environments is seamlessly scaled up to meet the 
uncompromising, fail-proof technology standards required for 
nuclear standby applications.
When grid cannot be a backup plan
KOEL 's involvement in the 6 MW engine development 
programme marks a category shift not just in product scale, 
but in the kind of customer the Company serves. Nuclear 
standby power is not a market entered lightly. The qualification 
standards, documentation requirements, and lifecycle 
commitments are of an entirely different order.
The Kudankulam nuclear power plant demands engines that 
may sit dormant for years, then start within seconds and sustain 
full load without hesitation. Fault tolerance is designed in from 
the first drawing. Quality traceability runs from raw material to 
commissioning record.
What KOEL has built is not just a 
product range; it is the engineering 
infrastructure to support the most 
demanding power users in the 
country. That is a position that 
takes years to earn and cannot be 
replicated quickly.
Engineering at scale
KOEL powers India's most unforgiving 
environments — from metro tunnels to 
nuclear standby systems.Built for what 
cannot run 
out of charge
There is a particular kind of engineering problem 
that most manufacturers choose not to solve. It lies 
at the intersection of extreme reliability, complex 
installation physics, and regulatory scrutiny. At KOEL, 
this space is increasingly bustling with activities.
Our 1,250 kVA product family reflects a deliberate 
move into premium, mission-critical power. At 
this scale, thermal management, load response 
stability, noise and vibration control, and multi-unit 
synchronisation are not optional; they determine 
whether the engine qualifies at all.

The export pivot
Premiumisation trendMarket context  
Strained US-China trade ties and the West's 'China+1' 
strategy have positioned India as a premier manufacturing 
and export hub, driving a 13% y-o-y growth in engineering 
exports. Concurrently, geopolitical uncertainties and energy 
transition mandates are accelerating global investment in 
alternative fuels and hybrid technologies. 
Impact  
These global shifts create sustained international demand 
for reliable, future-ready, and emission-compliant 
power platforms.
Our response
We are aggressively scaling our flagship Optiprime series in 
international markets. As the world’s most flexible generator 
platform in its class, it perfectly captures this global demand 
for versatile, next-generation infrastructure.
Market context  
Across the genset market, the demand is shifting towards 
medium and high horsepower products, driven by a growing 
share of data centers and large infrastructure projects in 
the overall demand mix. This shift is more structural rather 
than cyclical, as end-use applications become more power-
intensive and reliability-critical. 
Impact  
For manufacturers with a strong presence in higher-HP 
categories, this mixed shift is translating directly into 
margin improvement.
Our response
KOEL has accelerated its transition to HHP products, 
anchored by innovative offerings such as Optiprime and its 
ability to customise last-mile solutions. The flexible  
single-package design simplifies transportation and 
installation while enabling project-specific adaptations 
for acoustics, space constraints and site conditions. 
This solution-led approach, combined with a structured 
aftermarket programme, is helping us build recurring, 
margin-accretive revenue streams.KOEL operates at the intersection of India’s infrastructure growth, energy 
transition, and digital expansion. While regulatory changes and evolving energy 
dynamics throw up challenges, the Company is geared up to capitalise on 
premiumisation, industrial capex, and emerging energy solutions, enabling 
sustainable and resilient growth.Navigating a market  
in motionOperating context
Key market trends
Rising demand from infrastructure, data center, and industrial capex
Market context  
India’s $2.8 billion genset market has been growing at over 
10% per year to surpass $5.4 billion by 2030, driven by data 
centers, manufacturing facilities, hospitals, airports, and 
commercial real estate. 
Impact  
This increased demand is translating into sustained 
volume growth across the industry, with particularly 
strong momentum in high-horsepower and mission-
critical applications.
Our response
We are in process of expanding our manufacturing capacity 
and deepening our capabilities in HHP and mission-critical 
segments, while strengthening our order pipeline across 
industrial and infrastructure verticals. This positions us to 
benefit disproportionately from segments where demand 
is most resilient, driving bulk orders and ensuring long-term 
demand visibility.

India’s defence expansion 
Market context  
India’s defence sector is expanding on the back of stronger 
budgetary support, higher capital spending and a clear 
push for ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’. For FY 26–27, the Defence 
Ministry’s capital allocation is over ₹ 2.19 lakhs crores, and 
the overall defence budget stands at ₹ 7.85 lakhs crores. 
Defence industrial corridors have already attracted, while 
defence production and exports have reached record 
levels. The government has also highlighted the private 
sector and MSMEs as key contributors to this growth, with 
private players accounting for 45.16% of defence exports in 
FY 2025–26. 
Impact  
This environment is creating multi-year opportunities for 
private players that can supply mission-critical systems, 
specialised subsystems and reliable lifecycle support for 
defence applications. As procurement shifts more towards 
domestic sourcing, businesses are being asked to deliver 
higher reliability, faster deployment, tighter compliance 
and stronger supply-chain resilience. In practice, this is 
widening the role of private manufacturers from product 
suppliers to integrated solution partners.
Our response
We have positioned ourselves for this opportunity by 
incorporating Kirloskar Advanced Systems Pvt. Ltd. 
as a wholly owned subsidiary to handle specialised 
work in defence and railways separately from its core 
engines business. We have the engineering capability 
up to 10 MW and our defence portfolio covers land-
based projects, while our marine DG sets serve defence 
vessels and related applications. This gives us a focused 
platform to participate in India’s defence modernisation 
with project-specific, reliable power solutions.Structural demand drivers remain intact
Distribution and aftermarket transformationMarket context  
India’s genset market is underpinned by a set of structural 
forces that remain stable. Rapid urbanisation, sustained 
infrastructure build-up, expansion of telecom networks, and 
persistent gaps in grid reliability — all create a baseline of 
demand for gensets. 
Impact  
These structural drivers provide a long runway of steady 
demand visibility.
Our response
We are targeting overseas markets where grid reliability gaps 
create demand dynamics similar to those that have driven 
KOEL ’s domestic success, providing a natural hedge against 
any softness in the home market.
Market context  
India's industrial aftermarket and service ecosystem is 
expanding as customers increasingly prioritise equipment 
uptime, lifecycle value and maintenance efficiency. Growth 
in infrastructure, manufacturing and industrial equipment 
installations is driving demand for maintenance contracts, 
digital service platforms, remote diagnostics and predictive 
maintenance solutions. OEM-authorised service networks 
are also gaining importance as equipment becomes more 
technologically advanced and reliability-critical. 
Impact  
This shift is creating sustained opportunities for companies 
with strong service networks, customer engagement 
capabilities and digital service infrastructure. Businesses 
that can provide reliable aftermarket support, maintenance 
solutions and rapid response capabilities are better 
positioned to enhance customer loyalty, increase service 
penetration and grow recurring revenues. 
Our response
KOEL has strengthened its DABU through service penetration 
initiatives, dealer consolidation, digital transformation and 
focused AMC and extended warranty programmes. During 
the year, the business was restructured to enhance focus on 
major accounts, supported by dedicated service teams for 
key Powergen and industrial customers. 
We also expanded its whole-goods portfolio, strengthened 
customer engagement initiatives and invested in future-
ready service infrastructure, enabling a more responsive and 
integrated customer experience.

Data center expansion
Market context  
India makes up about a fifth of global data consumption but 
hosts less than 5% of the world’s data centers. The industry 
is on a swing. India’s digital infrastructure is expanding rapidly 
with enterprises investing heavily in data center capacity. It 
is estimated that India’s data center capacity is expected to 
grow from 1.5 GW in 2025 to 8–10 GW by 2030. Unlike most 
commercial applications, data centers operate under strict 
uptime requirements and cannot tolerate grid instability, 
making high-capacity backup power not a discretionary 
purchase but a core infrastructure requirement. 
Impact  
This non-discretionary nature of demand, combined with 
the scale and speed of data center investment across the 
country, is creating powerful and sustained tailwinds for 
premium, high kVA gensets. 
Push for indigenisation and infrastructure
Market context  
Government policy is playing an increasingly significant role in 
shaping the demand pattern in the industrial sector. Make-in-
India initiatives in defence, railways, and marine are driving a 
strong preference for domestically manufactured equipment. 
The government’s sustained commitment to investing in 
infrastructure across roadways, ports, energy systems, 
and urban development is generating large, long-duration 
project opportunities. 
Impact  
These policy-driven segments share common traits such 
as meaningful entry barriers in the form of technical 
certifications and indigenisation requirements that strictly 
limit the pool of suppliers, ensuring credibility. For companies 
that qualify, this translates into the access to high-value, 
relatively stable demand that is less exposed to the 
competitive intensity of open-market segments.Our response
We have made targeted investments in the capabilities 
and certifications required to compete credibly in 
defence, railways, and marine applications, developing 
indigenised product variants that meet the specific 
requirements of government procurement frameworks. 
The Company has partnerships with government 
agencies and PSUs to build the reputation and 
track record needed to capture a growing share of 
infrastructure-linked demand — a segment that we 
view as an important source of high-quality, long-
cycle revenue.
Our response
We have made the data center segment a strategic priority, 
treating data center expansion as a large opportunity in  
high-capacity, premium gensets.External environment
Stricter environmental scrutiny and decarbonisation push
Market context  
Beyond CPCB IV+, the broader trajectory of environmental 
regulation and corporate sustainability commitments 
is placing increasing pressure on diesel-based power 
generation. Consumers across sectors are facing growing 
scrutiny and this is beginning to shift the purchasing 
decisions in favour of lower-emission and hybrid power 
solutions. As a result, gas-based gensets and hybrid, 
solar and DG, configurations are emerging as the most 
immediate alternatives. 
Impact  
For the genset industry, this trend creates both a challenge 
and an opportunity. Manufacturers that remain anchored 
to conventional diesel products face the risk of gradual 
loss of demand as customers pursue greener alternatives. 
Those that invest in alternative technologies can position 
themselves to lead the next generation of the market, 
capturing early-mover advantage in segments that are 
growing rapidly and carry higher margins.Our response
KOEL has chosen to treat the alternate energy push 
as a strategic opportunity, instead of a threat. We 
have launched hybrid Optiprime series and it is 
gaining commercial traction and are investing in the 
development of hydrogen-ready systems to ensure 
it is positioned for the longer-term evolution of the 
market. We also provide engines designed to run on 
alternative fuels like ethanol, methanol, biodiesel, natural 
gas, biogas, and hydrogen. These include dual-fuel 
and flex-fuel solutions, helping industries reduce their 
carbon footprints.

that drive the impactMateriality assessment 
Materiality process
Building on the materiality assessment conducted in CY 23, 
KOEL undertook a reassessment in CY 26 to validate the 
relevance of previously identified ESG topics and ensure 
alignment with evolving stakeholder expectations, regulatory 
developments and the Company's changing business landscape.
We developed two sets of questionnaires to assess stakeholder 
expectations and the impact of the identified material topics.
We surveyed 76 internal and external stakeholders, including 
Board members, senior leadership, employees, customers, 
suppliers, investors, regulators, communities and knowledge 
partners, were engaged through structured surveys. Their 
responses were analysed using a defined scoring methodology, 
with the results directly informing the materiality matrix that 
shapes KOEL 's sustainability agenda and its sustainability 
strategy for its 2030 vision.

This topic was prioritised based on its relevance to both 
environmental impact and operational cost efficiency, and its 
growing importance to investors and regulators. We manage 
this through resource-efficient manufacturing, lean practices, 
segregation and authorised recycling of metal, oil, packaging, 
and e-waste, lifecycle thinking in product design, and monitoring 
systems with periodic audits to drive continuous improvement.
Human capital development 
Human capital development was identified as a material 
topic reflecting its centrality to the Company's strategic 
transformation into a technology-driven, diversified energy 
solutions provider. The assessment highlighted that the ability 
to attract, develop, and retain skilled and engaged talent directly 
determines the pace and quality of this transformation. Actual 
positive impacts include improved productivity, leadership 
continuity, and innovation capacity through structured 
capability-building and succession planning, while potential 
negative impacts, such as high attrition, skills gaps, and 
inadequate employee wellbeing could constrain growth and 
increase costs. 
This topic was prioritised as a strategic opportunity given its 
enabling role across business functions and its connection 
to human rights principles around fair employment, non-
discrimination, and safe working conditions. We address this 
through integrated learning and development programmes, a 
formal succession-planning framework, diversity and inclusion 
policies, wellness and engagement initiatives, transparent 
communication, and robust grievance-redressal mechanisms.
Climate action
The materiality assessment reflected growing expectations of 
environmental responsibility and the increasing influence of 
climate-related regulatory and transition risks to our operations 
and product portfolio. Actual positive impacts include improved 
energy efficiency, reduced operational costs, and enhanced 
market competitiveness from the development of low-emission 
and fuel-agnostic products, including the installation of  
8 MWp of captive solar capacity. Potential negative impacts 
include higher regulatory compliance costs, operational 
disruptions, and loss of market access arising from inadequate 
climate risk management or failure to transition to sustainable 
energy solutions.This topic was prioritised based on its dual risk-and-opportunity 
nature, its strategic alignment with our energy transition 
roadmap, and its material influence on long-term financial 
performance and stakeholder confidence. The Company 
manages this through energy efficiency measures, renewable 
energy adoption, digital energy monitoring, emission-compliant 
product development, ESG governance reviews, and alignment 
of capital expenditure and R&D priorities with climate objectives.
Human rights
Human Rights was identified as a material topic due to our 
heightened focus on fair employment, non-discrimination, and 
dignity at work across our dispersed workforce and extended 
value chain. Actual positive impacts include deeper employee 
trust, an inclusive organisational culture, and our positioning as 
a responsible and preferred employer, while potential negative 
impacts, such as lapses in fair employment, harassment, or 
inadequate grievance mechanisms could result in litigation, 
regulatory penalties, and reputational harm.
This topic was prioritised as a risk given the scale and diversity 
of our workforce and contractor engagements, and its direct 
connection to legal compliance and stakeholder trust. We 
manage human rights impacts through a formal human rights 
policy, a code of conduct, a POSH framework, an independent 
ethics and whistle-blower channel, regular awareness and 
compliance training, and the extension of this culture suppliers 
and partners through ethical sourcing standards. Our 2X3Y 
strategy has secured a firm foundation of operational excellence 
and financial strength. Anchored by this success, we are now 
pursuing our near-term aspirations and embarking on our most 
ambitious journey yet.Key material issues identified
(High and medium priority topics)
Corporate governance
The materiality assessment recognised that as we scale 
our operations across geographies and subsidiaries, robust 
governance becomes critical to managing compliance, 
reputational, and operational risks, while also presenting an 
opportunity to enhance stakeholder trust and long-term value 
creation. Actual impacts include improved investor confidence 
and strategic decision-making arising from strong oversight 
mechanisms, while potential negative impacts include regulatory 
penalties and reputational harm from gaps in governance. 
The significance of this topic was prioritised based on its dual 
risk-and-opportunity nature and its foundational role in enabling 
all other material topics. We address this through clearly defined 
Board roles and responsibilities, independent committees, 
integrated Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) framework, 
enterprise risk management, vigil mechanisms, and continuous 
regulatory monitoring.
Business ethics
The materiality assessment recognised that as we operate 
across domestic and international markets with a wide 
network of business relationships, maintaining ethical 
conduct is fundamental to business continuity, reputation, and 
compliance. Actual impacts include stronger stakeholder trust 
and disciplined decision-making through a stringent ethical 
culture, while potential negative impacts include financial losses, 
penalties, and reputational damage arising from lapses such as 
fraud, conflicts of interest, or non-compliance with the Code 
of Conduct. 
This topic was prioritised based on its broad applicability 
across the organisation and its direct bearing on our licence to 
operate. We manage this through a Code of Conduct applicable 
to Directors, employees, and suppliers, supported by structured 
policies on related party transactions, insider trading, whistle-
blower protection, and mandatory training, ensuring early 
identification and resolution of ethical concerns.
Occupational health and safety
The materiality assessment reflected the significance of 
occupational health and safety across machinery-intensive 
manufacturing facilities and field service operations. 
Stakeholder inputs, including those from employees and senior 
leadership, highlighted the direct link between workplace safety 
and operational resilience. Positive impacts include enhanced 
employee wellbeing, workforce productivity, and our record of zero injuries and fatalities across plants in the previous financial 
year. Potential negative impacts could be injuries, operational 
disruptions, regulatory non-compliance, and reputational harm 
from inadequate safety practices. 
This topic was prioritised based on its high relevance to human 
rights and employee welfare, as well as the regulatory and 
financial consequences of safety failures. We manage this 
through environmental, occupational health and safety policies, 
ISO 45001-aligned safety management systems, periodic audits, 
emergency preparedness drills, hands-on training on PPE and 
fire safety, and an embedded safety reporting culture.
Sustainable innovation
The materiality assessment recognised that tightening emission 
norms, technological advancement, and our strategic transition 
from a diesel-centric portfolio to a diversified energy solutions 
model make sustained innovation essential for regulatory 
readiness and competitiveness. Actual positive impacts 
include differentiated product offerings, improved emissions 
compliance, and stronger long-term market positioning, 
while potential negative impacts from delayed or inadequate 
innovation include increased compliance costs, loss of market 
access, and reduced competitiveness. 
This topic was prioritised as an opportunity, given its direct 
connection to our strategic transformation and future revenue 
potential. We manage this through structured in-house R&D 
investments, a technology roadmap focused on alternate fuels, 
emission-compliant platforms, modular designs, and digital 
integration with strong governance oversight ensuring alignment 
between innovation, manufacturing, and market objectives.
Circular economy
Circular economy was identified as a material topic through 
our 2026 materiality assessment, informed by stakeholder 
expectations around responsible resource use, intensifying 
regulatory focus on waste and material efficiency, and the 
environmental footprint of our manufacturing-intensive 
operations. Actual positive impacts include cost savings, 
reduced resource dependency, and lower environmental impact 
through practices such as 100% reuse of treated wastewater 
and plastic-to-fuel conversion. Potential negative impacts from 
inadequate circular practices include higher operating costs, 
regulatory non-compliance, and reputational risk arising from 
inefficient waste management or excess use of virgin materials.

CASE STUDY
Outcome
KOEL secured large-value orders in the data center segment, 
establishing a meaningful presence in one of India's 
fastest-growing infrastructure verticals. We strengthened 
our positioning in a high-growth, premium market where 
reliability and technical capability command significant 
pricing power. Critically, the integrated solutions model 
enhanced customer stickiness, making KOEL a trusted, long-
term partner rather than a transactional vendor.
Strategic impact
This initiative is a clear demonstration of the 2B2B model 
in action. By moving beyond product supply to become an 
integral part of the customer's infrastructure ecosystem, we 
captured higher value, deepened relationships, and built a 
scalable template for replication across other high-growth 
B2B verticals. 
Our 2B2B vision is redefining our growth trajectory, shifting 
the Company towards high-value, technology-driven, and 
partnership-led growth. By aligning strategy, investments, 
and execution with this vision, KOEL is building a future-ready 
business that delivers consistent, high-quality earnings and 
long-term stakeholder value.Enabling data center growth 
through high-capacity power 
solutions
Context
India's rapidly expanding data center ecosystem 
requires uninterrupted, high-capacity backup power 
solutions, creating sustained demand for reliable, high-
performance gensets.
KOEL's intervention
We leveraged our 2B2B strategy to position ourself as a 
comprehensive solutions partner, rather than a conventional 
equipment supplier. We developed and deployed high-
capacity HHP gensets tailored specifically for mission-
critical applications, ensuring the reliability and performance 
standards demanded by data center operations. Working 
closely with EPC contractors and data center developers, 
we embedded ourselves into the customer's value chain, 
offering not just product supply but end-to-end solutions 
encompassing installation support, commissioning, and 
lifecycle services.
Outlook
As we advance our 2B2B vision, the Company's growth strategy is anchored in ecosystem-led partnerships, technology-driven 
premiumisation, and disciplined capital allocation. Strong Powergen volume growth, significant export expansion, and a robust 
industrial order book position KOEL to pursue its $2 billion aspiration with confidence. With increasing aftermarket revenues 
enhancing cash flow stability, KOEL is building a future-ready, solutions-driven enterprise delivering consistent, high-quality earnings 
and long-term stakeholder value.Internationally, we believe every market needs a different approach. Our go to market approach is tailored to suit the local market 
dynamics. In MENA the appointment of GOEM is shaping well and in America the work is ongoing with Wildcat technologies. 
These investments are aligned with building technology leadership and scalable growth platforms.Objective
The goal to 'Grow' is anchored in its 2B2B strategy and involves 
the evolution of a transaction-led equipment manufacturer 
into an ecosystem-led solutions provider for OEMs, EPCs, 
and institutional buyers as well as indirect customers across 
the value chains. This positions KOEL as a critical enabler 
of infrastructure, industrial, and energy solutions, targeting 
sustainable, margin-accretive growth with improved return 
ratios and enables deeper integration, higher value capture and 
long-term partnerships. 
The core objective of the 2B2B strategy in the growth segment 
is to:
 z Enhance value per customer through integrated offerings 
spanning products, services, and lifecycle solutions. 
 z Increase the share of high-margin B2B segments, including 
industrial, infrastructure, and exports. 
 z Build scalable partnerships with OEMs and 
global partnerships.
 zStrengthen recurring revenue streams through aftermarket 
and service-led models. 
 z Drive premiumisation and technology-led differentiation.Performance
During the year under review, KOEL made significant 
strides in advancing its 2B2B agenda. We expanded our 
high-horsepower genset portfolio to cater to the spiralling 
demand for infrastructure upgrade and data centers, while 
simultaneously scaling our industrial business across defence, 
marine, and specialised sector applications. OEM partnerships 
were strengthened, particularly in export markets, through 
structured, long-term business models, and the aftermarket 
and service business grew meaningfully by leveraging our large 
installed base.
On the product front, new platforms such as our flagship 
Optiprime series and our advanced alternative fuel engines 
are driving our sustainable energy transition. We have actively 
chosen to treat the global shift towards alternative energy as a 
strategic growth opportunity rather than a market risk.

Outcome

have helped us move beyond our traditional identity as a diesel 
engine and genset maker. Our in-house Corporate Research

At KOEL, excellence is embedded in products, processes and 
people. In FY 25-26, we advanced our quality strategy based 
on five core pillars — People, Process, New Products, Data 
Analytics and Technology. This reinforces our commitment to 
deliver reliable, high performance solutions across industry, 
defence, marine and infrastructure sectors.
This year, a defining thrust was on transforming quality from 
a compliance function into a customer experience enabler. 
By building structured feedback loops across plants, OEM 
partners and field service networks, we systematically 
channelled real world performance data back into design 
and manufacturing, enabling faster resolution of field issues, 
smarter product decisions and a measurable improvement in 
customer satisfaction. This closed loop approach ensures that 
every insight from the field translates into a tangible quality 
enhancement at the source.
KOEL has also significantly expanded its use of data analytics 
and artificial intelligence; deploying these technologies across 
assembly lines, inspection checkpoints and supplier quality 
portals to achieve real time defect detection, predictive process 
control and smarter decision making at every stage of the 
value chain.
Reaffirming commitment to excel
During the year under review, KOEL intensified its focus 
on product quality through a combination of employee-led 
initiatives, advanced quality systems, and digital technologies. 
A total of 46 Quality Circle projects were undertaken across the 
GOEM units.
To improve product reliability and eliminate early-life failures, 
the Company revamped its Engine Quality Audit (EQA) process, 
putting them through extended endurance tests, followed by 
detailed teardown audits, enabling identification of latent defects 
and strengthening quality assurance across product platforms.
KOEL accelerated the adoption of Industry 4.0 quality practices 
through AI-driven computer vision and vision-recognition 
systems across assembly operations. These solutions automate 
defect detection, minimise human-error-related escapes and 
support near-zero-defect performance at critical control points. 
Complementing these efforts, the digitisation of BIS compliance 
tracking through a dedicated portal has enhanced visibility, 
accountability and real-time monitoring across the network.
Continuous improvement initiatives remained a key focus area, 
with 47 COPQ reduction projects helping lower the Cost of Poor 
Quality to 0.08% of sales, surpassing the Company's target. 
A dedicated Defective Part Analysis Centre (DPAC) was also 
used to strengthen field failure analysis, accelerate root-cause 
identification and improve corrective action effectiveness.

for partners contributing 2% or more to purchases/sales, aiming for 75% cumulative coverage.

collaborating closely with our partners, we aim to mitigate supply chain risks, ensure seamless regulatory preparedness, and 
drive collective sustainable growth.

Smart energy monitoring
We have firmed up monitoring by deploying IoT-enabled systems, 
energy-efficient compressors and SCADA-based solutions to 
enhance our ability to forecast, schedule, and regulate energy 
production while supporting fault detection and preventive 
maintenance activities. 
Compliance-driven engineering
To significantly reduce emissions during use, we integrated 
climate considerations into our product design through fuel-
agnostic and alternative-fuel engines and gensets compliant 
with CPCB IV+ and BS V standards. 
Due to the strict mandate, lower particulate matter, and NOx 
emissions for diesel gensets up to 800 kW, it has accelerated 
our transition towards advanced technologies like CRDI systems, 
after-treatment solutions, and dual-fuel configurations.
Driving circularity: LCA and waste stewardship
Following our FY 24-25 Life Cycle Assessment on our highest-volume engine platform, KOEL actively drives circularity 
through two key waste initiatives. First, the Kirloskar Nulife programme remanufactures field-returned engines to strict 
quality standards, extending lifespans and supporting customer carbon reduction. Second, the Company relies on recyclable 
packaging and metallic skids, whilst fully complying with Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) targets for plastic packaging 
and battery waste management.
Energy transition market readiness
Showing a strong commitment to responsible energy 
consumption, the Company balances strict regulatory 
compliance with resource optimisation across its product 
portfolio. By developing electronically controlled engines, 
integrating advanced after-treatment systems, and deploying 
emission-compliant technologies, we continuously minimises 
operational fuel consumption and lifecycle costs. We have 
proven our market readiness for the clean energy transition 
by commercialising alternative fuel solutions, including LPG-
powered gensets for retail use and ethanol-based variants for 
the telecom sector, ensuring eco-efficient performance across 
our entire footprint.Water management
KOEL has implemented a real-time water monitoring system featuring multiple water flow meters and live tank level sensors to 
track consumption across multiple sources. Centralised oversight through Bullfro Water Management Solutions ensures 24X7 
visibility, while in-house weather stations and piezometers enable efficient management of rainwater harvesting and groundwater 
levels. Additional conservation measures include the use of dry cutting machines in machining processes, reuse of air conditioning 
condensate for coolant preparation and installation of smart urinal O-rings to lower freshwater demand.
At KOEL, 100% of the treated wastewater is reused across manufacturing locations for processes such as flushing and irrigation, 
reducing freshwater withdrawal to support circular economy. We have deployed a 100-LPH Electric Evaporator in the Effluent 
Treatment Plant at its Nashik facility, treating 2 kilolitres of wastewater daily. It lowered our water intensity from 865.55 kL/million 
rupees adjusted to PPP to 696.91 kL/million rupees adjusted to PPP. 
We are transitioning from solvent-based to water-based paints to lower VOC emissions and minimise paint waste toxicity, while lean 
manufacturing reduces raw material, water, and energy consumption at source.18.21 %

Waste management
We believe that effective waste management improves environmental outcomes as well as operational 
and financial performance. Our multi-faceted approach focuses on proactive waste reduction at every 
stage of our operations. Although the overall waste increased, we achieved a meaningful annual 
decrease in waste intensity per rupee of turnover — 1.16 to 1.11 metric tonnes/million rupees.
Hazardous waste management
KOEL strictly monitors hazardous waste generation and tracks 
disposal pathways to guarantee proper handling. Oil waste is 
directed to recyclers, while authorised agencies manage specific 
hazardous categories through formal documentation systems 
in line with regulatory requirements. To ensure full compliance 
with the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) standards, the 
Company maintains dedicated on-site storage facilities and 
utilises trained personnel for all safe waste-handling operations.
Promoting circular practices
KOEL embeds circular economy principles throughout its 
operations to extend material lifecycles, recycle by-products, 
and close resource loops. Resource efficiency is maximised and 
dependency on virgin inputs is reduced by repurposing canteen 
waste for biogas generation and actively promoting the reuse of 
both materials and packaging.

  Environment
Environmental stewardship is integral to our commitment to sustainable development. Through initiatives focused on waste and 
wastewater management, biodiversity conservation, green space development, and environmental awareness programmes, we 
promote responsible resource management, ecological resilience, and a cleaner, greener future for communities. KOEL promotes 
environmental awareness and conservation through programmes such as KVER, Eco-Bazaar, workshops, guest lectures, and 
study visits. 
Our efforts aim to engage schools, colleges, and communities in meaningful environmental actions while showing responsible 
corporate leadership through tree plantation, waste management, and wastewater management projects.
Waste management
KOEL implemented an integrated waste management programme focused on Information, Education and Communication (IEC), 
operational process improvements, and social support mechanisms to strengthen waste segregation, enhance collection efficiency, 
and reduce landfill dependency.
Kagal waste management transformation
Context
In 2024, the Kagal Municipal Council faced challenges in 
waste segregation, landfill dependency, and inefficient waste 
processing. Low source segregation rates and inadequate 
waste management infrastructure highlighted the need for 
improved sanitation, sustainable waste practices, and greater 
community awareness.
KOEL 's intervention
As part of its CSR commitment, KOEL partnered with the 
Kagal Municipal Council to strengthen waste management 
and sanitation. The Company supported awareness 
campaigns in schools and communities, promoted 
source segregation, encouraged citizen participation, 
and helped improve waste processing infrastructure and 
operational efficiency.
Outcome
Within one year from August 2024, the initiative delivered 
significant results: the city's cleanliness ranking improved 
from 110th to 12th, source segregation increased from 30% 
to 80%, and waste processing facility Overall Equipment 
Effectiveness (OEE) reached 80%. Waste sent to landfills was brought down to zero from three 
loads, supporting a zero-landfill approach. The initiative also 
strengthened community awareness on waste management 
and earned KOEL a Gratitude Letter from the Kagal 
Municipal Council.
Strategic impact
The initiative demonstrates the power of industry-
government collaboration in advancing sustainable urban 
development. By improving waste segregation, eliminating 
landfill disposal, enhancing operational efficiency, and 
building community awareness, KOEL created a scalable 
waste management model aligned with circular economy 
principles and strengthened environmental stewardship in 
semi-urban India.

Wastewater management project at Shivaji University
As part of our commitment to environmental sustainability, KOEL 
provided CSR financial backing for an innovative, eco-friendly 
wastewater management pilot project at Shivaji University.
Project highlight
Nature-Based Solution: Modelled under the technical guidance 
of Shivaji University and implemented by the Laxmi Multipurpose 
Foundation, the project utilises phytoremediation—using 
Colocasia (Alu) and Canna (Kardal) plants along the Gomati 
stream to naturally filter organic pollutants without 
mechanical STPs.
Impact
Internal testing confirms improved water quality, which is 
recycled exclusively to irrigate 4,000 trees across 15 acres, 
successfully preventing untreated discharge from entering the 
Panchganga River.Biodiversity
Kagal biodiversity project
At KOEL, we are deeply committed to ensuring environmental 
sustainability and fostering climate resilience through the 
systematic enrichment of natural habitats and the holistic 
rejuvenation of local water bodies. Our initiatives at the Kagal 
Biodiversity Park focus on an intensive native plantation 
strategy, specifically designed to breathe new life into the 
ecosystem by introducing a rich matrix of indigenous flora 
that strengthens local bird and butterfly populations. A major 
cornerstone of this programme is the ecological restoration of 
the park's natural stream (nala) trajectories and water margins, 
where we are planting specialised, deep-rooting native species 
like Jamun, Arjun, and Erythrina to anchor soil banks, naturally 
filter water, and establish vital riparian corridors.
By collaborating with local institutions like the Forest 
Department nursery and the Naoroji Godrej Centre for Plant 
Research (NGCPR) to source climate-habituated, locally 
acclimated saplings, this initiative maximises plant survival rates 
and accelerates the recovery of the natural watershed.

and Refund) Rules, 2016 and its amendments thereon, all

14.  In accordance with the provisions of the Income Tax Act, 2025 
(“the Income Tax Act”) as amended from time to time, dividend 
declared and paid by a Company is taxable in the hands of 
shareholders and the Company is required to deduct tax at 
source (“TDS”) from dividend paid to the shareholders at the 
applicable rates. We shall therefore be required to deduct tax at 
source at the time of making the payment of the said dividend.
  Tax rate applicable to a shareholder depends upon residential 
status and classification as per the provisions of the IT Act. All 
shareholders are thereby requested to update any change in 
residential status and/or category with depository participants 
(in case of shares held in electronic form) or with the R & T 
Agent of the Company i.e. MUFG Intime India Private Limited 
(formerly known as Link Intime India Private Limited)  (in case 
of shares held in physical form).
  For the prescribed amended rates for various categories, the 
shareholders are requested to refer to the Finance Act, 2025.
  In this regard, the Company availed the facility for online 
submission of Tax Exemption forms online from RTA, MUFG 
Intime India Private Limited (formerly known as Link Intime 
India Private Limited)  wherein the shareholders can submit their 
tax-exemption forms along with other required documents.
  TDS will not be deducted in cases where a shareholder provides 
Form 121 (applicable only to Resident Individual shareholder), 
along with copy of self-attested Permanent Account Number 
(“PAN”) and Form 41, Tax Residence certificate (“TRC”) and 
No Permanent establishment certificate (“NPE”) (applicable 
only to Non-Resident Shareholders), provided that eligibility

18.  Securities Exchange Board of India amended relevant 
provisions of SEBI Listing Regulations, 2015 including 
amendments thereunder, to disallow listed companies from 
accepting request for transfer of securities, which are held in 
physical form, with effect from 1st Apri, 2019. The Members 
who continue to hold shares of listed companies in physical 
form even after this date, will not be able to lodge the shares 
with Company/its R & T Agent for further transfer. They will 
need to convert them to demat form compulsorily if they wish 
to effect any transfer.
  Pursuant to various SEBI Circulars, it is mandatory for the 
Company to issue shares only in demat form while processing investor service requests viz., issue of duplicate securities 
certificate, claim from Unclaimed Suspense Account, renewal/
exchange of securities certificate, endorsement, sub-division/
splitting of securities certificate, consolidation of securities 
certificates/folios, transmission and transposition. Further, 
SEBI substituted the earlier requirement of issuance of a 
physical ‘Letter of Confirmation’ (“LOC”) in lieu of duplicate 
share certificates, and the Company/the RTA are now required 
to directly credit the shares to the demat account in lieu of the 
share certificate while processing any of the aforesaid investor 
service requests.
  Special Window for Re-lodgement of Transfer Requests and 
Dematerialisation of Physical Securities
  Pursuant to SEBI Circular dated 2nd July, 2025, a special window 
was provided from 7th July, 2025 to 6th January, 2026 for  
re-lodgement of transfer requests lodged prior to 1st April, 
2019 and pending due to deficiencies. This facility has been 
extended vide SEBI Circular dated 30th January, 2026 effective 
from 5th February, 2026 until 4th February, 2027. Eligible 
shareholders may submit requisite documents within the 
extended timeline. Securities will be credited only in demat 
form and will be subject to a one-year lock-in, during which 
they cannot be transferred, pledged, or encumbered.

Board’s Report
To the Members
of Kirloskar Oil Engines Limited
Your Directors are pleased to present this 17th Annual Report together with the Audited Statement of Accounts for the Financial Year ended 
31st March, 2026 of Kirloskar Oil Engines Limited (“KOEL ” or “the Company”).
1. Company’s Financial Performance (Standalone)
  Your Company's sales from continuing operations for the financial year ended 31st March, 2026 stood at ₹ 5,603.85 Crores, as

including step-down subsidiaries during 
FY 2025-26 are as under:
i.  Kirloskar Americas Corporation, USA – (“KAC”)
  During the Financial Year under review, KAC’s revenue was 
contributed from Industrial, Powergen and Fluid Dynamic 
segments. KAC has stocking arrangements in Miami (FL) for 
engines, generating sets and spare parts. This enables faster 
deliveries of products to customers in North, Central and South 
America. The business environment in the USA was cautious 
after the announcement of tariffs of 25% in April 2025 which 
was increased to 50% in August 2025. This uncertainty 
had led cautious approach at customer end resulting into a 
lower demand coupled with some delays in procedures and 
documentation at the borders. The environment in Mexico was 
adversely affected due to continuously changing policies and 
interpretations holding up new investments and expansions. 
With introduction of higher capacity range through the 
Optiprime series, KAC successfully executed orders for a 
project in Belize and has offered Optiprime solutions for future 
projects in the Latam region. KAC is working on new avenues 
and ventures to succeed in these markets by pursuing to 
localize the products and meet local requirements. Relaxation 
of tariffs from 50% to 10% in the last quarter  boosted 
customer sentiments in the last quarter of the financial year, 
which saw some good traction from business both in the US 
and Latam region.
  KAC is playing a pivotal role for large scale projects by engaging 
with key players in the data centre segment to capitalise on 
unprecedented demand for larger capacity diesel and natural 
gas engine driven generator solutions in the US. Simultaneously, 
KAC has initiated projects with multiple OEMs in the US for gas 
engine long blocks in the high horsepower segment that should 
bring significant opportunities in the coming 3 – 4 years.
  Currently three (3) new families of engine are in process of Tier 
4 Final certification from US EPA and California Air Resources 
Board (“CARB”) and is expected to be completed in Financial 
Year 2026-27. These applications are being developed for 
Powergen and Industrial segment.
  KAC participated at National Fire Protection Association 
expo in United States of Americas. Stocking and packaging 
of engines and accessories in the US has led to a penetration 
amongst the OEMs in Americas region. KAC has also increased 
its service reach in different countries in Central and South 
America which has been leading to positive response from end 
customers in contractors in the region.ii.  Engines LPG, LLC dba Wildcat Power Gen, USA
  The business environment in the USA was cautious after 
the announcement of tariffs of 25% in April 2025 which was 
increased to 50% in August 2025. The same has resulted 
in lack of demand from distributor channel which has 
impact on Engines LPG LLC performance. In response, the 
organisation was right sized to align with business volume 
while prioritising foundational investments in enhancement 
of sales, service, support processes, and channel partner 
onboarding to build brand recognition. Technical milestones 
have showcased success, particularly with the Patriot series 
through multiple deliveries for mobile-rental applications and 
a promising product ramp-up cycle, alongside delivery of 
engineered solutions such as Natural Gas-driven engineered 
power solutions for agriculture application and drone-
charging applications for irrigation. Further showcasing 
these capabilities are notable solutions under development, 
including genset solution for mobile EV charging station and 
a portable eye hospital application.
  Engines LPG, LLC dba Wildcat Power Gen participated in the 
Powergen Show in Feb 2026 and showcased various products 
and solutions including Mobile Rental segment diesel gensets, 
Hybrid gensets with solar & battery integrated options and 
solutions where customer showed keen interest in our 
solution offerings.
  To deliver sustainable growth, Engines LPG, LLC dba 
Wildcat Power Gen is working towards a comprehensive 
strategic overhaul that includes transitioning to a new 
leadership team, enhancing the partnership with its key 
vendors, and aggressively revamping the channel strategy to 
establish robust distributor partnerships and increase key-
account focus. This strategy will be further reinforced by a 
broad investment in talent across sales, service, support, 
engineering, manufacturing, and assembly, which, combined 
with improved product availability, positions the organisation 
to course-correct with increased sales momentum in the 
coming quarters.
iii.  KOEL Fluid Dynamics Private Limited (“KFD”) 
[formerly known as La-Gajjar Machineries 
Private Limited ]
  KFD continued to expand its network both in domestic and 
international markets and geographies. During the year under 
review, KFD has expanded its network in regions like Africa, 
South East Asia, Latin America. The Sanand plant has reached 
at reasonable level of capacity utilisation after setting up of the 
new plant during the year. Transfer of B2C business segment 
of KOEL to KFD resulted in, improving value chain efficiency. 
Additionally, the Rajkot plant reached a fulfillment of more than 
80% capacity.

v. Kirloskar International ME FZE, UAE (“KIME”)
  During the Financial Year under review, KIME started its 
operations from 1st October, 2025 after receipt of its VAT 
registration. KIME’s revenue drivers are Firefighting Engines, 
Industrial Engines and Spares in Middle East and North Africa 
territory. KIME has stocking arrangements in UAE for engines 
and spare parts. This enables faster deliveries of products to 
OEMs (customers).
  KIME faced serious business revenue challenge due to loss 
of our largest OEM account to Chinese manufacturer, which 
created a significant short-term gap. The team responded 
with focused execution across the broader portfolio through 
accelerated engagement with existing and new customers 
across assigned territory. Due to which, KIME not only stabilised 
the business but also delivered growth across other accounts.
  During the financial year, KIME successfully established new 
Industrial revenue streams in the Construction and Automotive 
segments, with key wins in cement bulkers and mobile road 
sweeper applications. Also drove market expansion by 
acquiring new customers (OEM’s) in strategic markets such 
as Saudi Arabia, Egypt, and Turkey thus, strengthening our 
regional footprint
  KIME expanded after-sales network by onboarding new  
service partners in Egypt and Saudi Arabia, significantly 
improving service reach, response time, and customer support 
in these critical markets.vi.  Arka Fincap Limited (“AFL ”) - Step-Down 
Subsidiary
  AFL is a Non-Deposit Taking Systemically Important Non-
Banking Financial Company (“NBFC”). It operates as a subsidiary 
of Arka Financial Holdings Private Limited (“AFHPL ”), which in 
turn, is a subsidiary of Kirloskar Oil Engines Limited (“KOEL ”). AFL 
is professionally managed and specialises in providing structured 
term financing solutions to Retail, Corporate, Real Estate, and 
Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprise (“MSME”) borrowers.
  With a customer-centric approach, a seasoned management 
team, and diligent monitoring of loan assets, AFL has witnessed 
significant growth since the inception of operations in fiscal 
year 2020. It operates in 3 main business segments: SME 
Lending, Wholesale Lending and recently launched Secured 
Retail Financing.
  The launch of our Secured Retail vertical represents a defining 
shift in Arka Fincap’s strategy, prioritising asset granularity 
and long-term balance sheet stability. As a primary growth 
catalyst, this segment leverages Secured Business Loans 
and Pre-Owned Wheels financing to bridge the credit gap for 
the MSME sector, fostering a more diversified and resilient 
portfolio. The speed of execution in Secured Retail has been 
remarkable; within a single year, we established a presence 
across 7 states with a robust network of 100+ Secured Retail 
branches. This rapid scale-up is powered by a dedicated 
team of over 1,000 retail professionals whose local insights 
have driven deep market penetration. Strategically, the retail 
segment now contributes ~9% of Arka’s total AUM. More 
importantly, it is fundamentally shifting our asset composition 
toward greater granularity. By reducing concentration risk 
and increasing the number of touchpoints, we are building a 
scalable foundation that ensures long-term stability.
  Within SME vertical, we provide higher ticket Loans against 
Property to Small and Medium Enterprises. Our Wholesale 
Lending business comprises of Corporate Lending, Real 
Estate & Urban Infra Lending and Syndication (Distribution) 
Business. Corporate Lending division excels in tailoring 
bespoke loans to precisely fit the unique needs of medium 
and large corporations. The Real Estate and Urban Infra 
Lending division is dedicated to facilitating the growth of India's 
infrastructure and real estate sectors by providing either partial 
or complete capital infusion. With a keen focus on catering to 
the requirements of its esteemed clients, the division ensures 
a smooth and seamless process from initiation to completion. 
Syndication business offers comprehensive solutions to 
corporate clients encompassing project finance, capital 
expenditure, general corporate needs, last mile financing,  
and subordinated structured debt. Through advisory, 
syndicating, selldown, and co-lending strategies spanning 
various sectors, it ensures tailored financial assistance for 
every requirement.  Overall, Arka Fincap continued its upward trajectory in FY 26, 
achieving a 9.5% y-o-y growth in AUM to reach ₹ 7,947 Crores. 
This growth was achieved alongside a deliberate focus on 
increasing granularity, ensuring a high-quality and resilient 
portfolio for the future.
  With a customer-centric approach, a seasoned management 
team, and diligent monitoring of loan assets, upholding our 
motto of 'Lend wisely, serve deeply,' we closed the year with 
a GNPA of ~1.2%. This asset quality underscores our ability 
to achieve rapid scale upholding our rigorous underwriting 
standards that define our business.

13.  Risk Management, Internal Audit and 
Internal Control Framework
  The Board recognises the importance of sound internal 
controls and risk management practices to good corporate 
governance. The Board is responsible for the governance of 
risk and ensures that management maintains a sound system 
of risk management and internal controls, to safeguard the 
interests of the Company and its shareholders. All material 
decisions of the Board take into relevant consideration the 
nature and extent of risks which the Company is willing to take 
in achieving its strategic objectives and value creation. The 
Company’s internal control system is commensurate with 
the nature of the business, size and complexity of operations 
covering all businesses and functions of the organisation. In line 
with the commitment of a high standard of compliance with 
accounting, financial reporting, internal controls, corporate 
governance and auditing requirements and any legislation 
relating thereto, the Company has a Code of Business Conduct 
applicable to Company personnel covering a wide range of 
business practices and procedures. This includes, but is 
not limited to, compliance with laws, rules and regulations, 
avoidance of conflicts of interests, practicing ethical behavior, 
ensuring integrity of financial statements, protection of 
information, intellectual property and technology, diversity 
and inclusion and prevention of harassment and violence. 
The Company’s risk management process is designed to 
facilitate identification, evaluation, mitigation and review of 
risks which may affect achievement of objectives. It is aligned 
with the strategy deployment processes of the organisation. 
A risk-based audit plan on a yearly basis is approved by the 
Audit Committee. Significant observations and progress of 
implementation of the action plan are reported to and reviewed 
by the Audit Committee. The enterprise risks and their 
mitigation plans are presented by the risk owners to the Risk 
Management Committee. The Enterprise Risk Management 
(“ERM”) framework is aimed at effectively mitigating the 
business and enterprise risks through strategic actions. The 
mitigation plans for enterprise and business risks are reviewed 
and updated on a periodic basis to the Risk Management, 
Audit Committee and the Board of Directors of the Company. 
The risk management process which has been established 
across the Company, addresses major types of risks which 
are at enterprise and business level. The risks are reviewed 
with respect to the likelihood and impact following a balanced 
bottom-up and top-down approach covering all businesses 
and functions of the Company. The review of the risks is done 
based on changes in the external environment, which have a 
=== page 73 ===
Kirloskar Oil Engines Limited | A Kirloskar Group Company Annual Report 2025-26138 139
Corporate Overview Statutory Reports
 Financial Statements
significant bearing on the risks. The Risk Management Policy 
developed by the Company guides the risk management 
processes which is in line with size, scale and nature of the 
Company’s operations. The risk management process works 
at various levels across the organisation. It is an ongoing 
process and forms an integral part of management focus. The 
Risk Management Committee oversees risk management 
standards, practices, and systems. The Risk Management 
Committee periodically reviews the effectiveness of the ERM 
system within the Company and evaluates the adequacy and 
effectiveness of administrative, operating, and accounting 
controls used by the Company. In addition to this, the control 
self-assessment framework complements the internal audits 
and helps the employees to monitor the internal controls they 
are responsible for. This system aids in building a robust control 
environment across the organisation.

  The Company has adopted a Vigil Mechanism/Whistle Blower

employees of the Company and persons dealing with the 
Company to report to the Chairman of the Audit Committee 
or Ethics Committee or Ethics Ombudsman any instance of 
unethical behaviour, actual or suspected fraud or violation of 
the Company's code of conduct or leakage of Unpublished 
Price Sensitive Information (“UPSI”), by any person, who 
is in possession of UPSI, to any other person in any manner 
whatsoever, except as otherwise permitted under the SEBI 
(Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015, or any other 
instance. The Whistle Blower Policy/Vigil Mechanism and 
Process flow has been made accessible to all employees.
  The Company adopted online Ethics Helpline to report any 
suspected violations of code of conduct or any other ethical 
concerns or raise concern under Whistle Blower/Vigil 
Mechanism, through email/hotline/webmode. The Company 
had a tie-up with an independent third party specialist service 
provider “Integrity Matters” to handle concerns reported. The

A. Conservation of Energy
  The coming year, our commitment to efficiency and 
environmental responsibility takes on a new urgency. The 
recent, stricter government pollution norms, such as the CPCB 
IV+, Bharat Stage VI emission norms and Corporate Average 
Fuel Efficiency (“CAFE”) standards, are not just regulatory 
requirements; they are a clear call to action for our industry 
and a vital step towards ensuring cleaner air and a healthier 
planet for future generations.
  As a leader in engine manufacturing, we recognise our 
significant role in this transition. The industrial sector accounts 
for a substantial portion of national energy consumption, 
and our products have a direct impact on environmental 
quality. Therefore, our response to these challenges must be 
proactive and innovative. We can also focus on how our internal 
manufacturing processes can become more energy-efficient 
and compliant with environmental regulations.
  We at Kirloskar Oil Engines Limited, leverages Environmental, 
Social and Governance (“ESG”) principles to create both 
financial and non-financial value. By prioritising sustainable 
practices like local procurement, recycling and reusing of waste 
etc. KOEL reduces operational costs and enhances efficiency, 
leading to improved financial performance. ESG initiatives 
also strengthen brand reputation, attract socially conscious 
investors, and foster customer loyalty. KOEL 's commitment to 
ESG not only drives profitability but also ensures sustainable 
growth, aligning the company with global best practices and 
stakeholder expectations.
  Identifying and continuing the journey on sustainability, KOEL 
is recognised at State and National level for continuous efforts 
and fantastic results in Energy Conservation drive. KOEL 
once again, emerged as strong leader in Energy and Water 
conservation initiatives and bagged “Excellent Energy efficient 
unit award and National Energy Leader award” organised by CII 
and awarded with “Gold rating in India Green Manufacturing 
Challenge, Diamond trophy for consecutive performance and 
Runner up in APEX and Water awards by CII”.I.  The steps taken for energy conservation and 
its impact
